title: Theologumena Arithmeticae (Greek)
author: Iamblichus (de Falco ed)
description: Theologoumena Arithmeticae (The Theology of Arithmetic), attributed to Iamblichus, in the Greek critical edition by Vittorio de Falco (Leipzig: Teubner, 1922). This anonymous late-antique compilation, probably drawing heavily on Iamblichus and on lost works by Nicomachus of Gerasa and Anatolius, is the chief surviving text of Pythagorean number mysticism. It treats each of the numbers one to ten, the Monad, Dyad, Triad, Tetrad, Pentad, Hexad, Heptad, Ogdoad, Ennead and Decad, describing their mathematical properties together with the gods, virtues, elements, cosmic principles and symbolic names associated with each (for instance the Tetrad as the source of the tetraktys and the Decad as 'universe'). De Falco's edition, with Latin preface and apparatus, is the standard text. It underlies later Neoplatonic, Renaissance and modern esoteric numerology.
